body.x: Seyoung Information & Telecommunication will participate in the world’s largest technology exhibition CES 2020 opening in Las Vegas on Jan. 7-10 to showcase its bi-directional wireless transceiver WiWi.

Seyoung Information & Telecommunication is a company specializing in manufacturing, repairing and maintaining wired and wireless communication equipment. Major business partners are telecommunication operators such as Samsung Electronics, LGU + and SKBB, and can repair more than 4,000 types of communication equipment and have more than 40% of domestic market share.

WiWi has three outstanding features compared to competing products. First, it is compatible with Bluetooth earsets. Both wired and wireless earsets can be used, and it supports 100% wireless communication.

Second, wired and wireless repeaters for extending communication distance. It can be used in a space that requires more than the maximum communication distance of the product, and supports a communication distance of more than 2 km. Third, the noise canceling function supports clear calls even in noisy spaces. In addition, built-in speaker and microphone can be installed, and the ergonomic design and simple design improve the quality of communication products.
The official said, "Seyoung I&T currently has major bases in Europe and Japan. In 2020, we are planning to target the new markets in the US and China.

We are in the process of acquiring the FCC and SRRC, which are the standard certification of the target country, and are planning to enter the new market in full force by completing this by the first half of 2020.” He continued, “We are looking for big distributors and brokers specializing in IT and telecommunication devices, or sports referees who use the products the most, and related sporting goods distributors."

The world’s largest IT show CES shows the trend of the global consumer electronics industry at a glance. It is hosted by Consumer Technology Association (CTA) and is held every January. AVING NEWS has reported the most news on CES, MWC, and IFA, the world's three major tech exhibitions for the past 13 years. It is sending special reporters to CES this year to report major issues in the global market and introduce outstanding Korean companies to the world.
